title: Sublime Convergence
subtitle: What I learned from reading about Constructivism and Surrealism at the same time.
seo_title: Constructivism Surrealism: Sublime Convergence of Mountains, Waves, and Technicolor Skies
seo_description: A generative series blending constructivist structure with surreal motion: curling mountains, crashing waves, and technicolor cloud fields illuminated by radiant light.
thumb_alt: Swirling clouds, rolling mountains, reflective lakes, and crashing waves in vivid color.

tiles: The pieces I couldn't stop looking at
challenge: Constructivism and Surrealism feel like opposites at first — one wants structure and purpose, the other wants dreams. But the more I read, the more they seemed like two honest answers to the same question about what art should do in a modern world. I wanted to see what happened when I tried to hold both in one image.
approach: I researched each movement separately, then drafted many variations where the composition had a Constructivist spine but the content behaved like a dream — mountains that curl into waves, skies that feel too vivid to be real. I kept the ones that felt like they'd learned from both.
result: Six pieces I'm genuinely proud of, and that taught me something about both movements. They're available as prints for anyone who responds to that particular mix of structure and strangeness.
